text:
maria_support: Hey team — escalation from Ashley at CorpWave. After they switched to our VPCE (interface endpoint) their API calls intermittently 502 or fail TLS. Customer says behavior started after enabling Private DNS for the endpoint and moving their k8s egress through a Windows-based on-prem proxy.

ashley_ce: repro steps I gave them: 1) create interface endpoint vpce-0a1b2c3d in us-east-1, enable Private DNS 2) add VPC route -> endpoint in each app subnet 3) on-prem DNS resolves api.redwood.com to 10.12.34.56 (vpce ENI IP) 4) requests go through corp-proxy -> outbound to VPCE IP 5) ~20% of requests get 502 and TLS errors. curl -v output attached: 
```
* Connected to 10.12.34.56 (10.12.34.56) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* SSL: certificate subject name 'internal-vpce-xxx' does not match 'api.redwood.com'
* TLS handshake error
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

maria_support: They also collected a short tcpdump from the on-prem proxy. Key bits: ClientHello SNI always 'api.redwood.com' but backend TLS cert sometimes CN 'internal-vpce-xxx' returned. Sometimes golden handshake happens and they succeed.

sam_eng: :eyes: sounds like a split-horizon / backend routing mix where some backend servers present our public cert and some present endpoint-level cert. Two quick checks: 1) Is our NLB doing TLS passthrough or TLS termination for this endpoint? 2) Are there multiple target groups (e.g., internal NLB targets + public targets) that might be mixed by route policy?

kevin_infra: Confirming infra: the VPCE is backed by an internal NLB in the Red team account. We use TLS passthrough at the NLB (no cert termination) so TLS should go end-to-end to the instance. We have an ALB in front of some regions for hosted traffic with a different cert chain — if traffic is accidentally routed to the ALB we could see cert mismatch.

remy_sre: Two hypotheses: hairpinning/asymmetric routing and SNI rewrite at on-prem proxy. If request goes on-prem -> VPCE -> NLB -> backend, the backend sees source IP as the VPCE ENI (hairpin) OR the on-prem proxy IP depending on path. If response path goes via NAT gateway or a different AZ, connection may be routed to a different pool that has a different cert. Ask customer to test direct curl from a bastion in the VPC (bypassing on-prem proxy) to the VPCE IP to see if behavior reproduces inside the VPC.

ashley_ce: They tried a curl from a vpc-bastion and saw 0 failures (all succeed), so appears to be specific to on-prem path.

sam_eng: Ok that rules out our internal mixing. Next check: does the on-prem proxy rewrite SNI or terminate TLS? The curl -v they shared implied proxy is doing TLS inspection sometimes (we saw replaced cert CN 'internal-vpce-xxx'). Ask them to disable TLS inspection for api.redwood.com or preserve SNI and do passthrough.

ashley_ce: Customer says their proxy only inspects traffic for destination hostnames in a specific egress allowlist. api.redwood.com is allowed, but the proxy may still do opportunistic TLS inspection for certain backend IPs. They also noted Windows k8s nodes have multiple NICs and SNAT via a corporate NAT for egress.

kevin_infra: Multi-NIC + SNAT can cause source IP changes. If some requests get SNATed to a different public IP, the return path might be forced through a different egress device that hits a different peering/edge and that edge might be terminating or rewriting TLS (ugh). Ask for pcap showing IP and TCP 3-way handshake so we can trace which upstream sees which source IP.

remy_sre: Also check VPCE DNS configuration: If their local resolver sometimes returns the private IP and sometimes returns public IP (split-horizon misconfig), that would flip between proxy paths. Confirm `dig +short api.redwood.com @their-resolver` during failures.

ashley_ce: Provided quick dig logs: every lookup from their on-prem resolver returns 10.12.34.56 consistently. But their proxy does an internal ORIGIN lookup and sometimes re-resolves via public resolver (weird).

maria_support: Suggested immediate mitigations to customer: 1) Add api.redwood.com to proxy TLS passthrough/no-inspect list 2) Ensure on-prem egress preserves SNI header and does not terminate TLS for that host 3) Temporarily route a subset of traffic from on-prem through a VPC bastion/proxy to confirm no proxy influence 4) Share pcap + proxy config with us for deeper trace.

ashley_ce: They applied TLS passthrough exemption and reported error rate dropped from ~18% to ~1%. They will capture a pcap for the remaining failures and share.

sam_eng: Follow-ups for platform: We should add a KB note for customers with on-prem proxies + VPCE: common culprits = TLS inspection, SNI rewrite, multi-egress SNAT asymmetry, split-horizon DNS. Include commands to test: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:10.12.34.56 https://api.redwood.com/` and `dig +short api.redwood.com` and `tcpdump -n -s 0 -w trace.pcap port 443`

remy_sre: I'll open an internal ticket to add a short doc and checklist. For this thread I recommend we ask for: pcap from on-prem proxy, proxy TLS inspection config, route table configs, and nat device logs. I'll also check our NLB target certs for any misconfiguration but bastion tests already looked good.

ashley_ce: Thanks everyone — customer is now stable after passthrough change. I have their account id and will attach pcaps when they come in. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Great — closing tentative, leave open until we get pcaps and KB article draft. :white_check_mark:
